notes:
S11 sprint work: the module 'sprint planning documents' (docs/epics/**/STATUS.md) had no test suite, and one of them lied twice in a single session — the S11 STATUS file carried the ambiguous RUN label, then showed two work arms (T859, T860) as ACTIVE after both had closed. This task builds that suite: tools/regression-status-doc-truth.sh, wired into `zig build test` in build.zig next to the T848 store-census block.

FOUR ARMS, each validated red-first where the discipline requires it:
A. RED against REAL history — the check run against the S11 revision at 2efaac3 (committed 2026-08-24 16:17:04, one edit before the seat's correction at 88f5ef5) FAILS, naming both rows (T859, T860) and both states (doc label ACTIVE vs store status done). This is the actual historical defect, not a seeded one: the red was observed against the real pre-correction document and the real store before the script was finalized.
B. GREEN at HEAD — the live check passes against the three current STATUS.md documents and the live store (exit 0), and prints the census: 3 documents exist; 4 rows cross-checked (all four S11 arm rows: T857/T858/T859/T860 ARMS vs store done); 12 task rows reported UNKNOWN; documents with no legend: S01-process-ownership/pass1 and S06-orchestration-refactor.
C. Seeded control — one label change (T857 ARMS -> ACTIVE) in a scratch copy of the HEAD document goes red, naming the row and both states. Hermetic scratch store.
D. No-false-alarm control — a document whose rows genuinely match the store (done/in_progress/dispatchable vs DONE/ACTIVE/not-started) is SILENT: exit 0, zero FAIL lines. Asserted, not merely quiet.

Measured wall time: 0.276 s for all four arms (fast tier; brief budget 45 s).

DESIGN DECISIONS (each reasoned, per the honesty requirement):
- The label->store-status mapping is derived from each document's OWN declared legend (each legend label's prose is classified by lifecycle keywords), never a hardcoded vocabulary. The legend itself is detected structurally: backtick-quoted labels whose descriptions are separated by '·', with at least one description naming a lifecycle state. S06's first paragraph contains both '·' and backtick tokens (a commit hash and a model id) and is correctly NOT read as a legend.
- A document with no parseable legend is reported UNKNOWN (rows unchecked), not failed — an unmeasurable document is not a lying one (brief constraint). S01 and S06 are such documents; their 12 task rows carry no store verdict.
- The undeclared-label check (every label used is declared) applies to rows that name a store task. State cells on rows with no task ID (e.g. S11's 'grade (untracked)' rows reading 'awaiting dispatch') are prose about the seat's next action, not store assertions; failing them would make HEAD red, which the brief's acceptance says must be green.
- Existence accepts rows in the archive as well as the live store: S06 cites T771, which was retired and lives in archive.json. A retired row is recorded and verifiable.
- Suffixed citations resolve by stripping: T556-stats -> T556, T802-consolidation-sprint -> T802, T441-AUDIT matches its own row. A bare base with no such row (T441 when only T441-AUDIT exists) still fails as a citation of nothing.
- Named (non-numeric) task ids like ORCHA-FLASH cannot be distinguished from prose when missing from the store, so existence is verified only for the ids the store itself knows; a missing named id is inherently undetectable and is a stated blind spot, not a claim of coverage.
- The check reads the live store but never writes it; all mutation lives in the seeded hermetic arms (scratch stores in the disposable /tmp scratch tree). No status document was edited to make the check pass — HEAD was green as committed.

TEST-FIRST RECORD: the red evidence (Arm A) is the real historical defect at 2efaac3, observed failing before the final script shape; Arms C and D prove the instrument can still fail and can stay silent. The script is the instrument and its test in one file, per the brief's single deliverable.

WHAT THE BRIEF DID NOT REQUIRE, DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: scanning 'sibling documents' beyond STATUS.md (the brief's primary module surface). No sibling under docs/epics currently asserts task states, and scanning every epics document for T-ids would flag historical prose; the STATUS.md glob is the defined surface and the census reports exactly that.

REPORT CENSUS (at HEAD, 2026-08-24): status documents exist: 3. Rows cross-checked against the store: 4 (all verified). Task rows reported unknown (no legend / archived): 12. Documents with no legend: S01-process-ownership/pass1/STATUS.md, S06-orchestration-refactor/STATUS.md. No document currently fails any check; the regression's job is to keep it that way.
